db.title: Database
db.noneHint: Open an existing Certana database or create a new one to get started.
db.heldBy: The database is currently opened for writing by {{user}}@{{host}}. You can read but not change anything.
db.sharedHint: Shared mode: rollback journal with exclusive locking. Only one Certana instance writes at a time; others open read-only.

session.title: Session
session.unlockHint: The issuing CA key is decrypted into memory for this session and locked again automatically after the idle timeout.

profileHint.server: Apache, nginx and other TLS servers. Needs DNS names or IP addresses.
profileHint.client: Mutual TLS, VPN and device authentication.
profileHint.smime: Signing and encrypting e-mail. Needs an e-mail address.

ca.name: Name
ca.nameHint: Display name inside Certana, e.g. «Root CA 2026».
ca.empty: No certificate authorities yet. Start with a root ceremony or import an existing root.
ca.selectHint: Select a CA on the left.
ca.rootOfflineHint: The root key is not stored in this database. It lives in the encrypted root bundle and is only needed for ceremonies: signing an issuing CA or renewing the root CRL.
ca.crlUrlHint: Embedded into certificates issued by this CA. Serve the exported CRL file at this URL.
ca.aiaUrlHint: URL where clients can fetch this CA's certificate.
ca.noKey: This issuing CA has no stored key – certificates cannot be issued.

ceremony.title: Root CA ceremony
ceremony.warnText: The root key is the most valuable secret of your PKI. Create it on a trusted machine, ideally with the network disconnected, and store the bundle on removable media.

warnList.1: Disconnect from the network for the duration of the ceremony.
warnList.2: Prepare a USB stick (or two) for the encrypted root bundle.
warnList.3: Choose a long passphrase and store it in a password manager or a sealed envelope.
warnList.4: After the ceremony, only the root certificate stays in the database.

ceremony.ack: I understand that the root key will only exist in the bundle file.
ceremony.algoHint: ECDSA P-384 is recommended; RSA 4096 for maximum compatibility.
ceremony.rootCrlUrlHint: Where the root CRL will be published (lists revoked issuing CAs).
ceremony.passphraseHint: At least 16 characters. It encrypts the bundle and the key inside it. There is no recovery if it is lost.
ceremony.bundleHint: Choose where to write the encrypted bundle (*.certana-root), e.g. on a USB stick. Keep a second copy in a safe place.
ceremony.doneText: The certificate was registered in the database. The private key exists only in the bundle.
ceremony.backupReminder: Copy the bundle to a second medium now and verify that you can open it (CA → Create issuing CA checks bundle and passphrase).
ceremony.signHint: Signing requires the root bundle and its passphrase. The root key is decrypted only for this operation and wiped afterwards.

import.title: Import root CA
import.keyPassHint: Only for encrypted PKCS#8 keys. Convert other formats with `openssl pkcs8 -topk8`.
import.bundleHint: The imported key is re-wrapped into a Certana root bundle protected by a new passphrase.
import.certOnlyHint: Issuing CAs will be created as CSRs for external signing.

intermediate.title: New issuing CA

flows.ceremony: Sign now with the root bundle
flows.csr: Create a CSR for external signing
flows.import: Import a signed certificate for a pending CSR

flowHint.ceremony: Generates the issuing CA key, stores it encrypted in the database and signs the certificate with the root bundle.
flowHint.csr: Generates the key (encrypted in the database) and writes a CSR you can hand to an external root. Finish later with «Import a signed certificate».
flowHint.import: Completes a pending CSR with the certificate returned by the external root.

intermediate.importNameHint: Must match the name used when the CSR was created.
intermediate.passphraseHint: Protects the issuing key in the database. You enter it to unlock the CA for a session.
intermediate.csrDoneHint: Have it signed by the external root, then come back and choose «Import a signed certificate» with the same name.

crl.title: CRL
crl.hint: Each CRL is valid for {{days}} days. Publish a new one after every revocation and before the current one expires.
crl.needsUnlock: Unlock the issuing CA to sign a CRL.
crl.notExported: No CRL export directory configured – the CRL is stored in the database only.
crl.rootHint: The root CRL lists revoked issuing CAs. It is signed with the root bundle.
crl.expired: The latest CRL expired on {{date}}. Clients may reject certificates until a new CRL is published.
crl.serveHint: Serve the exported CRL file at the configured distribution point: {{url}}

trust.title: Distribute the root certificate
trust.hint: Export the root certificate (PEM/DER) and install it on clients. Only the root is distributed; servers deliver the issuing CA in their chain.

firefox.title: Firefox
firefox.cmd: Settings → Privacy & Security → Certificates → Import…  (or policy: security.enterprise_roots.enabled = true)

cert.subject: Subject
cert.noIssuingCa: You need an unlocked issuing CA before issuing certificates.

wizard.title: New certificate

sansHint.server: Comma-separated. The first name becomes the CN.
sansHint.smime: The e-mail address the certificate is for.

wizard.needHost: Server certificates need at least one DNS name or IP address.
wizard.needEmail: S/MIME certificates need an e-mail address.
wizard.cnHint: Leave empty to use the first name above.
wizard.keyGenerateHint: Key and certificate are exported together; the key is stored encrypted.
wizard.keyCsrHint: The private key stays on the server; paste or load its CSR.
wizard.ed25519Warn: Ed25519 is not supported by all browsers and TLS clients.
wizard.csrPolicy: Only the public key is taken from the CSR. Names come from the previous step; usages and validity from the profile.
wizard.validityHint: Browsers accept server certificates up to 398 days. Maximum for this profile: {{max}}.
wizard.issueHint: The certificate is signed with the unlocked issuing CA. You will be asked for its passphrase if it is locked.

export.title: Export
export.noKeyHint: This certificate was issued from a CSR – the private key is not in Certana.
export.keyPerms: The key file was written with permissions 0600. Install it as root and keep it that way.

revoke.title: Revoke
revoke.warning: Revocation is permanent. Publish a new CRL afterwards so clients learn about it.
revoke.notInCrl: not yet in a CRL – publish one

renew.title: Renew
renew.hint: Issues a new certificate with the same names and profile.

dashboard.nothingExpiring: Nothing expires in the next 30 days.

settings.crlExportDirHint: Published CRLs are written here as <ca>.crl and <ca>.crl.pem (e.g. a web root).
settings.autoLockHint: Unlocked issuing CA keys are wiped from memory after this idle time.
